clauses.old_judgment_reason: Terminated by statutory repeal on 1935-06-14. The report command (paragraph 6) directs the Code Authority to submit to the Administrator a study of hours, rates of pay and conditions three months after the code's effective date, as a condition of the approval. The three-month period is a report deadline and is not an end; the command depends on the code and the Code Authority the code creates. The order states no period, condition or date of its own, so it has no own-terms end. Its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I: under 3(b) the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, a violation in or affecting interstate commerce was an unfair method of competition, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 (49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, approved June 14, 1935) provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed' and states no later effective date, so the approval's prospective operative effect ended when the resolution was approved. Actor: the Congress by Senate Joint Resolution 113. The date is the resolution's approval date, not a general rule's default: the repeal reaches this command because the command had legal effect only through the repealed provisions. June 16, 1935 is not an end (section 1 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936). Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization recorded in source_notes, not an end date.

clauses.old_judgment_reason: First end: express revocation on 1934-10-12. EO 6871 paragraph 1 provides 'That paragraph numbered 1 of Executive Order No. 6861, dated September 28, 1934, be and it is hereby revoked.' Actor: EO 6871. The stay's own stated end was October 15, 1934 (inclusive; exclusive reading: when that day began), later than the revocation. EO 6871 paragraph 2 then stays the same amendments to and including December 1, 1934 by its own command; that is a later event, not an extension of this stay.

Exhausted by performance on 1934-10-10. EO 6871's recital states that the Board 'duly appointed' the three named persons as the committee under this order and that the committee 'on October 10, 1934, did report its recommendations' after hearing protests and investigating; the command (appoint forthwith, hear, report on or before October 10, 1934) was fully performed on the report date, with the appointment falling between September 28 and October 10. Actor: the National Industrial Recovery Board and its committee, as recited by EO 6871. EO 6871 paragraph 3 continues the committee with new instructions on its own authority; that is a later event, not a continuation of this command.

Exhausted by performance no later than 1934-10-12. EO 6871, dated October 12, 1934, recites the committee's report of October 10 and states 'I ... do hereby approve and adopt the report and recommendations of said committee', so the recommendations had reached the President by October 12; the transmittal therefore occurred between October 10 and October 12, 1934. The exact day is not stated; the clause is dated at the day by which the evidence shows performance. The order does not say that the Board itself carried the document; the command's object, that the recommendations reach the President, was accomplished. Actor as recited: the Board.

applications.summary: Route for narrow reconciliation; affirmative October 1934 evidence supports the old core account, but exact transmission date and actor are not expressly established.
applications.scope_check: Three commands: paragraph 1 stays specified amendments; paragraph 2 requires Board appointment and committee hearing/investigation/report; paragraph 3 requires Board transmission to the President. The closing understanding concerns a later presidential decision; it does not erase the three commands. EO6871 expressly revokes only paragraph 1 and separately continues the committee for new work.
applications.earlier_end_check: EO6871 paragraph 1 expressly revokes the stay October 12, before its inclusive October 15 own-term endpoint. Its new December 1 stay is a later distinct command. The recital expressly states appointment occurred, hearings/investigation occurred and recommendations were reported October 10. Presidential adoption on October 12 establishes possession by that date; it does not state the exact transmission day or expressly identify the Board as the delivery actor. The known interval and inference must remain distinct from an exact first_end date. May 27/June 14 1935 are later than these demonstrated October events and need not be used to rescue this case.
applications.independent_command_check: Paragraph 2's specified mission can be treated as performed from affirmative recital; the committee's existence is a surviving institutional consequence continued by EO6871, not proof of an unperformed old mission. Paragraph 3's object (recommendations reaching the President) is strongly evidenced by adoption; literal Board transmission and timing are narrower unresolved facts. No demand for an exact appointment date should erase the observed appointment interval.
applications.savings_check: The report and committee are surviving results of completed acts; EO6871 continues the committee with further work and establishes a new stay. Nothing warrants treating report delivery as committee dissolution. The old report mission can be functionally completed while the same institution survives.

applications.scope_check: Code approval is expressly subject to an Administrator report within 120 days of code effectiveness, covering first 90 days, sufficiently detailed to permit presidential determination whether modification/elimination is needed. applications.earlier_end_check: June 14, 1935 is the supported repeal event for code approval/prescription/enforcement powers, not a proven universal first cessation. June 16, 1935 was replaced as the scheduled Title I expiry; April 1, 1936 is a conditional outer statutory limit, not this member's demonstrated first end. The code effective date is absent; February 14 signature is not automatically that date. Both 90-day measurement and 120-day report/determination periods require the actual trigger. The deadline is not a sunset.
applications.independent_command_check: The Administrator must report to the President on past effects, particularly Article V. Section 3(a) permits reporting conditions, yet recipient/actor and subject call for administrative-performance inquiry. Later NRA review of past code experience shows why loss of code enforcement alone cannot prove this report ended. Reserved presidential power is not evidence of actual exercise.

Res. 113's proviso do not establish universal surviving liabilities, universal agreement conversion, or continuation of every administrative direction.
